flawed_step: Step 6: Distinct greedy colors do not imply that the corresponding vertices are adjacent.
counterexample: Let T have vertices a,b1,b2,c1,c2,c3,c4,r and edges ar, b1b2, b2r, c1c4, c2c3, c3c4, c4r. This is a tree, so chi(T)=2. In the order a,b1,b2,c1,c2,c3,c4,r, greedy assigns colors 1,1,2,1,1,2,3,4, using 4 colors although chi(T)+1=3.
assessment_summary:
1. Fix a graph G, a vertex order, and let k=chi(G). [Justified: these are arbitrary objects covered by the statement.]
2. Choose a proper k-coloring of G. [Justified: this exists by the definition of chromatic number.]
3. Suppose, seeking a contradiction, that greedy assigns color k+2 to some vertex v. [Justified: this is the appropriate negation to investigate.]
4. Then v has previously colored neighbors x_1,...,x_{k+1} whose greedy colors are respectively 1,...,k+1. [Justified: otherwise a smaller available color would have been assigned to v.]
5. Two of x_1,...,x_{k+1} receive the same color in the chosen proper k-coloring. [Justified: k+1 vertices are distributed among only k colors.]
6. Those two vertices must be adjacent because their greedy colors are distinct. [Not justified: vertices can receive distinct greedy colors because of different earlier neighborhoods, even when they are nonadjacent.]
7. This adjacency contradicts their receiving the same color in a proper coloring. [Not justified: the asserted adjacency comes only from the false Step 6.]
8. Therefore greedy uses at most k+1 colors. [Not justified: the attempted contradiction has failed.]
9. To determine whether the statement is nevertheless true, define T with vertices a,b1,b2,c1,c2,c3,c4,r and edges ar, b1b2, b2r, c1c4, c2c3, c3c4, c4r. [Justified: this specifies a finite simple undirected graph.]
10. T is a nonempty tree and hence is bipartite with chi(T)=2. [Justified: it is connected with eight vertices and seven edges and contains no cycle; its edge implies chi(T)>1.]
11. Process the vertices in the order a,b1,b2,c1,c2,c3,c4,r; greedy assigns colors 1,1,2,1,1,2,3,4 in that order. [Justified: b2 sees color 1; c3 sees color 1; c4 sees colors 1 and 2; and r sees colors 1, 2, and 3.]
12. Thus greedy uses 4 colors on T, while chi(T)+1=3. [Justified: this follows from Steps 10 and 11.]
13. Consequently, the universal statement is false. [Justified: Step 12 supplies a graph and processing order violating it.]
